method.dwelling_key: site_id + apartment_id (the record states apartment_id is only unique per site)
method.dwelling_filter: unit_usage RESIDENTIAL only; dwellings with <2 valid areas or <15 m2 indoor net area dropped
method.deduplication: Floors that reuse the same plan give identical apartments (same area_ids). Each distinct layout (set of area_ids) is counted ONCE; n_apartment_instances shows how many real apartments the layouts stand for
method.label_schemes: Annotations use either explicit labels (BEDROOM / LIVING_ROOM / LIVING_DINING) or a generic ROOM label. If LIVING_* is present and BEDROOM is not, ROOM = bedroom. If BEDROOM is also present, ROOM = study. Layouts with ONLY generic ROOM labels ("--R", about 23%) have no reliable living/bedroom split, so they are EXCLUDED from all groups (see sensitivity_generic_room_scheme)
method.bathroom_split: Swiss BATHROOM areas are split by fixtures: shower or bathtub -> bathroom (full); toilet without shower/bath -> wc; no fixtures -> sanitary_nofixture
method.shape: short/long side and aspect ratio = minimum rotated rectangle of the room polygon (plans are often rotated). rectangularity = area / that rectangle; near_rectangular_subset (rectangularity >= 0.9) is the fairest comparison for the villa's rectangular rooms
method.doors: Doors carry no room id in the data, so they are matched geometrically: a DOOR / ENTRANCE_DOOR polygon within 5 cm of a room whose boundary runs >= 0.20 m along it; the 2 best rooms are kept. doors_per_room counts DOOR + ENTRANCE_DOOR. See qa.opening_matching_counts: ~98.6% of interior doors match exactly 2 rooms
method.open_connections: Two rooms <= 2 cm apart sharing >= 0.5 m of boundary (annotator "area splitter", no wall between them), e.g. an open kitchen to living
method.shares_wall_or_boundary: rooms <= 0.6 m apart whose 0.3 m buffers overlap along >= 1.0 m (i.e. back-to-back across a wall), plus all door/open links
method.connection_probabilities: connections.<kind>[t1][t2] = share of t1 rooms with >= 1 link to a t2 room. ENTRANCE = dwelling entrance door, EXTERNAL = door to a space outside the dwelling other than the entrance. link_pair_share = share of all links by room-type pair
method.swiss_room_count: n_rooms_swiss = number of ROOM + BEDROOM + LIVING_ROOM + LIVING_DINING areas (Swiss "Zimmer" count, half-rooms ignored). rooms_ge4 therefore mostly = 3 bedrooms + living
method.circulation: corridor/hall (CORRIDOR, CORRIDORS_AND_HALLS, LOBBY, FOYER) + STAIRCASE areas inside the dwelling / indoor net area (indoor = all non-outdoor, non-technical areas). Circulation inside open-plan living rooms is not counted

derived_types.bedroom_master_proxy: largest bedroom of a dwelling with >= 2 bedrooms
derived_types.bedroom_secondary: the other bedrooms of such dwellings
derived_types.bathroom_ensuite: full bathroom with a direct door/open link to a bedroom
derived_types.bathroom_shared: full bathroom without such a link
derived_types.hall_entrance: corridor that holds the dwelling entrance door

method.percentiles: linear-interpolated percentiles over rooms (room stats) or dwellings (dwelling stats), one weight per unique layout

living: ROOM (only in generic-label sensitivity block: largest ROOM)
bedroom: ROOM (when LIVING_* is labelled and BEDROOM is not)
study: ROOM (when BEDROOM and LIVING_* are both labelled)
bathroom: BATHROOM with SHOWER or BATHTUB fixture
wc: BATHROOM with TOILET but no SHOWER/BATHTUB
sanitary_nofixture: BATHROOM with no sanitary fixtures drawn
stair: STAIRCASE (area inside the dwelling; rare, see dwelling.internal_stair_fixture)
laundry: WASH_AND_DRY_ROOM (never inside a dwelling in this data, see dwelling.in_unit_washing_machine)

caveats: Apartments, not villas: Swiss multi-family flats (median indoor net area about 84 m2 overall, about 106 m2 for rooms_ge4) are much smaller than a Gulf 4-bedroom villa. Room SIZES in a villa will often sit at or above the Swiss p75-p95; treat high-side deviations as informative, not as errors.

Regional and cultural bias: Swiss (mostly German-speaking-region) housing from Archilyse clients, i.e. institutional and investor stock, not a random sample. No majlis, maid, driver or prep-kitchen rooms; laundry is communal in the basement; en-suite bathrooms are rare (about 8% of dwellings, 11% for rooms_ge4) and the bathrooms-per-bedroom ratio (median 0.5) is far below Gulf villa practice (usually >= 1). A villa exceeding the Swiss p95 on sanitary ratio is normal.

Generic-label layouts (about 23% of unique layouts, only ROOM labels) are excluded from all groups; the sensitivity block shows their bedroom and bathroom areas are similar but heuristic "living" rooms are smaller, so living-room stats describe explicitly labelled (more recent) plans.

Door and adjacency relations are recovered geometrically (doors have no room id in the data); about 1.3% of interior doors and about 9% of entrance doors could not be matched within 5 cm, so door counts are slight undercounts.
Open-plan circulation is invisible: circulation_share counts only labelled corridor/hall/stair areas, so open-plan layouts show lower shares.

Internal STAIRCASE areas are rare (maisonettes draw stairs as a fixture inside a corridor or living area). Stair footprints come from merged fixtures per floor and may describe only the part of a flight drawn on that floor.
Shorter side and aspect ratio use the minimum rotated rectangle; for L-shaped or irregular rooms this overstates the usable width. Use near_rectangular_subset when checking rectangular villa rooms.
Floor repetition is removed (one count per unique layout). n_apartment_instances gives the undeduplicated apartment count.
